title: Triad voice leading
description: Common tones, smallest motion, and smooth paths on one string set.

cards.front: What is voice leading on a three-string triad?
cards.back: How each note of one chord moves to a note of the next. Treat each string as a voice. Motion on a string is the fret change in half steps.

cards.front: What does smooth voice leading mean?
cards.back: Notes stay put when the next chord contains them (common tones) and otherwise move by a half step or a whole step.
A pitch class that belongs to both chords. Keep it on the same string and fret when you can.

cards.front: When do two triads share notes?
cards.back: When their roots are a third apart (two common tones) or a fifth apart (one). Roots a step apart share none.

cards.front: In C, name common tones: C–Am, C–Em, C–F, C–G, C–Dm, F–G.
cards.back: C–Am: C E. C–Em: E G. C–F: C. C–G: G. C–Dm: none. F–G: none.

cards.front: Give the four-step method for connecting two chords.
cards.back: 1. Spell both. 2. Mark common tones and keep them. 3. Move remaining voices to the nearest new-chord note. 4. The inversion you land on is a consequence, not the target.

cards.front: How do you measure smoothness on one set?
cards.back: Add the half steps each string moves. A guide, not a law — sometimes you accept a leap for a good bass or a melody note on top.

cards.front: Is sliding the whole shape the same as independent voice leading?
cards.back: No. If all three voices move the same amount the same way, that is a slide. Useful, but not the same as holding common tones.

cards.front: Which tendency tones should you keep when you can?
cards.back: A leading tone goes up a half step to the tonic. A chord’s seventh goes down.

cards.front: Give the smooth C–Am–F–G–C path on 4–3–2 (frets and notes).
cards.back: C 10 9 8 (C E G). Am 10 9 10 (C E A). F 10 10 10 (C F A). G 9 7 8 (B D G). C 10 9 8. Total motion 12; hand stays frets 7–10.

cards.front: In that smooth path, what do the bass and top voices do?
cards.back: Bass (string 4): C C C B C. Top (string 2): G A A G G.

cards.front: Same progression in root position each time: about how much more travel?
cards.back: C 10 9 8, Am 7 5 5, F 3 2 1, G 5 4 3, C 10 9 8. About 42 half steps vs 12 on the smooth path.

cards.front: From C 10 9 8, compare G as 9 7 8 vs 12 12 12.
cards.back: 9 7 8 = B D G, motion 1+2+0 = 3, keeps G. 12 12 12 = D G B, motion 2+3+4 = 9. First is smoother.
Am 7 5 5 (A C E). Dm 7 7 6 (A D F). E 6 4 5 (G♯ B E). Am 7 5 5. Total 10. G♯ resolves up to A.

cards.front: In G major, start G as 9 7 8 (B D G). Smooth Em–C–D–G?
Smoothest F after C E G (10 9 8) on 4–3–2?
cards.back: C F A as 10 10 10. Total motion 3: C stays, E→F up 1, G→A up 2.

cards.front: Smooth Dm–G–C from Dm 7 7 6, total motion at most 7.
cards.back: G as 9 7 8 (motion 4, common tone D), then C as 10 9 8 (motion 3). B resolves to C.

cards.front: When would you pick a root-position hop instead of the smooth path?
cards.back: On purpose, for power or clarity. Same harmony, larger jumps, thicker less-connected sound.
